clue.text: Rough winds in which doctor's held on to hat

indicators.note: held on to says the doctor's letters are gripped inside the shuffled word
winds, read as twists and turns, tells us to reshape the letters of rough

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a standard abbreviation for a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor clings to his hat in a blustery gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' looks like the weather of the surface, and 'winds' like gusts, but 'winds' is the signal to reshape the letters while the doctor sits inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A homburg is a felt hat with a dented crown and curled brim, so it is an example of headwear.

clue.text: Handled bag put earlier in large meeting room

indicators.note: put says one word is placed somewhere
in says the earlier word goes inside the meeting room

parts.note: a hall is a large room for meetings
old means of an earlier time

explanation.surface: A bag with handles is left in a big conference room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handled' looks like a verb, but it means having handles.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft bag with handles for carrying belongings.

clue.text: China's competitor, not very important

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a friend

indicators.note: not says the very letter is removed from the competitor

parts.note: a competitor is a rival

explanation.surface: China's commercial rival is not a big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Material means significant or relevant, as in a material fact, which is something important.

clue.text: Where one finds Chicanos and, say, rising employment

parts.note: Chicanos are Mexican Americans, found in the USA

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upward, so the letters are turned

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A question about where Mexican Americans live and their growing jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the act of using something, and employment can mean use, as in the employment of force.

clue.text: Port sauce on duck -— eaten by French, mainly

indicators.note: eaten by says the sauce and duck go inside the French word
mainly means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Gallic means French

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the sauce above the duck

parts.note: lip is cheek or sauce, insolence
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shown as O

explanation.surface: Port wine sauce over duck is eaten by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims the last letter from the French word, and 'eaten by' puts the sauce-and-duck pair inside what is left. 'Port' looks like wine but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli is a port on the Dardanelles in Turkey, scene of the 1915 campaign.

clue.text: Old boy in bar knocked over fat cat

indicators.note: knocked over means toppled, so the whole assembly is read backwards
in places the old boy within the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to ban
OB is the usual abbreviation for an old boy of a school

explanation.surface: A rich old boy gets floored in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives BOBAN; 'knocked over' turns it round. 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb to prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a very wealthy, self-important person; nabob originally meant a Mughal governor.

clue.text: Report — by no means one extremely funny

parts.note: not means by no means
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: extremely picks out the end letters of funny

explanation.surface: A news item that is not at all amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: To notify is to inform or tell officially, a synonym of the verb to report.

clue.text: Here's good luck, going to head up troops fighting at 4, but not at the end

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, turned round

parts.note: nob is slang for head

indicators.note: not at the end says the last letter is removed

parts.note: ANZAC troops from Australia and New Zealand fought at Gallipoli, the answer to 4 down

explanation.surface: A toast of good luck to the officer about to lead troops into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at 4' refers to the answer to 4 down, Gallipoli, where the ANZACs fought.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a windfall or a run of great good fortune, from a rich vein of ore.

clue.text: Hard worker on railway, like porter

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the worker above the railway

parts.note: a busy bee is a byword for a hard worker

explanation.surface: A railway porter works hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like the railway worker of the surface, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark beer, so something like porter tastes or smells of beer.

clue.text: One strike following another quickly

indicators.note: following says one blow comes right after the other

parts.note: another strike is a second chop
a chop is a cutting blow

explanation.surface: Blows rained down one after another, fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom urging speed, meaning hurry up or quickly.

clue.text: Large present wrapped for composer

indicators.note: wrapped says the large letter is enclosed, like a gift inside paper

parts.note: to present a show is to host it
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big gift is wrapped up for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift (encouraged by 'wrapped'), but it is the verb, as a TV presenter hosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was an English composer, best known for The Planets suite.

clue.text: Suddenly everybody's in agreement about Conservative

parts.note: everybody means all

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the agreement phrase goes round the Conservative letter

parts.note: to be at one is to be in agreement

explanation.surface: Without warning, everyone agrees on the Tory position.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means simultaneously or without warning, the same as abruptly.

clue.text: Couple must accept affair's ending, that is plain

indicators.note: must accept says the couple takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a couple is a pair

indicators.note: ending picks out the final letter of affair

parts.note: ie, id est, is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like an adjective meaning obvious, but it is the noun, a stretch of flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast flat grassland, a kind of plain, especially in North America.

clue.text: Early days of city's wingers revealed by home supporter

parts.note: in means at home
a fan is a supporter

indicators.note: wingers are the players on the edges, so only the outside letters of city are taken

explanation.surface: A home fan spots the club's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: Football colours the surface: city's wingers are its first and last letters, CY.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is the earliest period of life, and by extension the first stage of anything.

clue.text: Bear right after fishing port, area in uproar

indicators.note: right after means immediately following, so the bear goes straight after port and area

parts.note: Hull is a fishing port in Yorkshire, England
Baloo is the bear in Kipling's Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A bear in a fishing port causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like a direction letter R, but 'right after' means immediately after. HULL is a fishing port on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A hullabaloo is a noisy commotion or fuss, the same as an uproar.

clue.text: Lost for words after losing head in crudest brawl

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter is removed

parts.note: rawest means most crude or unrefined
a ruck is a rough scrum or brawl

explanation.surface: Someone is speechless after a fight in which they took a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes R off RAWEST, giving AWEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone awestruck is so overwhelmed with wonder that they are speechless.

clue.text: Name included in chat about report

indicators.note: included in says the name letter is placed inside the turned word

parts.note: gab is idle chat

explanation.surface: A name crops up in conversation about some news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns GAB into BAG; 'included in' puts N inside it. 'report' looks like news but is a loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp sound of a gun or explosion, which a bang is.

clue.text: Share essays about Henry V

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a go, so essays means goes

explanation.walkthrough: 'essays' looks like school papers but is the verb, attempts; 'Henry V' gives HAL plus V.
explanation.definitionFit: To go halves is an idiom meaning to split something equally, to share it.

clue.text: Say, four in revolt prepare to fight

parts.note: four is a square number, the say marking it as an example

explanation.surface: Four rebels get ready for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is to adopt a fighting stance, as boxers do before a bout.

clue.text: Hand over identity card while away

definitions.meaning: to hand something over is to give it on to someone
a permit or ID card that grants entry is a ...
to while away time is to spend it idly

explanation.surface: A soldier surrenders his ID while on leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: to give over, an entry permit, and to spend time idly.

clue.text: Attempt to mislead sons over own dodgy position

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the sons letter on top

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: dodgy, meaning unsound, tells us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: a job is a position or post

explanation.surface: A father deceives his sons about his shady line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A snow job is American slang for a persuasive deception or smooth-talking con.

clue.text: Abandon lie-in and rush madly about? Without question!

madly about says the letters are thrown about wildly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Should one skip a lazy morning in bed and dash around? Certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without question!' looks like an exclamation of assent, but 'Without' means outside: the rearranged letters wrap Q.
explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish is to give up or let go of, a synonym of to abandon.

clue.text: US motor, lead-free sort, lively when climbing

explanation.walkthrough: 'lead-free' looks like unleaded petrol but drops the K of KIND.
explanation.definitionFit: IndyCar is the American open-wheel racing series and its cars, an example of an American motor.

clue.text: Queer fish gathering under dam on river

clue.text: Complaint from bore about pants

clue.text: An Englishman Abroad — private, making fresh start

clue.text: Run over kid going around dirt

clue.text: Buddhist scripture is just great (but oddly ignored)

clue.text: When smitten just aim to capture men's hearts, say

clue.text: Compere in Europe once taking me back

clue.text: Tough set-back for child, and almost another

clue.text: I'm knocking off chips behind King's Head
